metaDescription: Six walker tray tables compared on handle fit, stated weight rating, fold design and cup holders, for eating and carrying from room to room.
introParagraphs: A walker tray table is meant to double as a tabletop, which means it has to hold a plate steady, keep a mug upright and sit securely on the handles. People shopping for a tray table usually want a place to eat, read or do a puzzle, not just a carrying shelf, so surface size, edge height and cup holder spacing matter more than they do for a basic bag.

We evaluated six tray tables from Medline, StrongArm, DMI, NOVA, Bluestone and Medical King, based on product specs and buyer feedback. They range from a hinged flip tray to flat slide-on panels, and weight ratings run from 5 to 10 pounds where stated. Fit numbers, fold behavior and capacity carried the most weight in our scoring.
Because a tray changes how a walker handles, check the stated weight rating and ask a clinician or physical therapist to confirm that a tray suits your frame.

products.name: Medline Walker Flip Tray Table with 2 Cup Holders
products.description:
Medline sells a flip tray that folds when you are not using it and attaches to most standard folding walkers without assembly. It has two cup holders and a half inch edge, and the maker states a 10 pound capacity. The listing gives the size as 22 x 12 x 6 inches and says the tray itself weighs 3 pounds.

The flip action is the draw, because the surface can be tucked out of the way and brought up when you want to set down a plate. The tradeoff is weight, as 3 pounds is nearly double the NOVA at 1.7 pounds, and the listing is light on fit measurements, so check your walker against the product page. It is labeled universal for standard folding walkers only.

Expect a quick install and a simple wipe-clean surface, with the hinge adding some bulk when folded. Compared with the NOVA, which shares the 10 pound rating, the Medline folds but weighs more. Against the DMI at 5 pounds, it carries double the stated load.
products.bestFor: Standard folding walkers where a tray that flips away is handy.
pros: Folds when not in use to save space
Stated 10 lb capacity
Two cup holders and a half inch edge
No assembly needed
cons: Heavier at 3 lbs than flat trays
Few fit measurements in the listing

products.name: NOVA Walker Tray Table with Spill-Proof Raised Edges
products.description:
NOVA offers a deep 16 x 22.75 inch surface that fits a full dinner plate, with two 2 7/8 inch cup holders and a half inch raised edge. The tray supports 10 pounds yet weighs only 1.7 pounds. It slides over the handles of a standard 2-button folding walker, with or without front wheels.

The tradeoff is a narrow compatibility window. The listing says it does not fit 1-button paddle folding walkers and asks for 16.75 inches between handles and 11.5 inches of handle depth. If you match those numbers, you get the best combination of surface, capacity and low weight in this guide.

It lifts on and off easily, wipes clean and needs leaning storage because it does not fold. Compared with the Medline at 3 pounds, the NOVA is lighter, though the Medline flips. Against the Bluestone at 21 x 16 inches, it has a deeper tray and a stated capacity.
products.bestFor: Meals on a 2-button folding walker with the right handle spacing.
pros: Deepest surface here at 22.75 inches
10 lb rating at only 1.7 lbs
Spill-proof edge runs all the way around
Published handle spacing makes checking easy
cons: Rigid, so it does not fold

products.name: Bluestone Walker Tray Table with 2 Cup Holders
products.description:
Bluestone is a gray high-impact polystyrene tray measuring 21 x 16 inches. Handle slots of 11.75 x 2 inches let it slide over the walker handles, and two 2.75 inch cup holders sit 8.5 inches apart. A half inch raised edge helps keep items from sliding off.

It has no moving parts, so there is little to break or adjust. The tradeoff is that the listing offers no weight capacity and no folding feature, so you must stay conservative with loads and find a place to store it. The cup holders are sized for typical mugs, so very wide tumblers may not fit.

Ownership is simple, with wipe-clean plastic and a drop-in fit. Compared with the NOVA, Bluestone is a little shorter front to back at 21 inches overall but lacks a stated rating. Against the Medical King bamboo tray at the same 21 x 16 inches, the Bluestone is plastic and does not fold in half.
products.bestFor: A plain, no-fuss tray for light loads on standard folding walkers.
pros: Published slot and cup holder dimensions
Simple slide-on fit, no parts to adjust
Half inch edge keeps plates in place
Wipes clean quickly
cons: No weight rating in the listing

products.name: DMI Walker Tray with Cup Holders for Folding Walkers
products.description:
DMI publishes the clearest fit window of the group, covering walkers about 16 to 19 inches from handle to handle with handles no longer than 11.5 inches and 1.5 inches wide. The tray measures 21 x 16 x 1 inches, has two cup holders and raised edges, and slides over the handles without tools.

The listing states a capacity of 5 pounds and says it is not compatible with extra wide or bariatric walkers. That rating is half of the NOVA and Medline, so it suits light loads such as a book, a snack and a drink. The maker also encourages you to check the size guide in the listing images before ordering.

It is plastic, wipes clean and stores flat against a wall. Compared with the NOVA at 10 pounds, the DMI is more tolerant on handle spacing but carries less. Against the Bluestone at the same 21 x 16 inch footprint, it adds a stated range and rating, which gives you more to verify.
products.bestFor: Light loads on walkers whose handle gap falls in a 16 to 19 inch range.
pros: Wide stated 16 to 19 inch fit range
Clear handle length and width limits
Raised edges and two cup holders
No tools or assembly
cons: Not for extra wide or bariatric walkers

products.name: StrongArm Walker Tray with Cup Holder
products.description:
StrongArm focuses on shape, with angled handle openings and a contoured user-side curve that lets the tray sit closer to your body. The maker says this helps it stay secure, and that the cup holder sits away from hinge points so it does not interfere with folding the walker. It is made of tough, high-grade plastic and finished in neutral gray.

The tradeoff is that the listing does not publish dimensions or a weight rating, so you cannot confirm fit by measuring. Attachment loops allow you to hang a storage tote, but the bag is sold separately. The single cup holder gives less beverage capacity than the two-holder trays.

It installs by slide-on and wipes clean. Compared with the Medline at 10 pounds, StrongArm states no rating but should not block folding. Against the NOVA, which states exact handle gaps, StrongArm is vaguer on fit.
products.bestFor: Users who fold their walker often and want the tray out of the hinge area.
pros: Contoured edge sits closer to the body
Cup holder placed away from hinge points
Loops let you hang a tote
Tough, lightweight plastic
cons: No dimensions or weight rating published

products.name: Medical King Bamboo Walker Tray Table
products.description:
Medical King uses bamboo for a 21 x 16 inch tray that folds in half. Raised edges help reduce spills, and precision-cut slots let it rest on the handles. The finish looks more like furniture than medical equipment, which many households prefer in a living room.

The listing is open about limits. Cup holders are meant for lightweight cups and may not fit every size depending on walker bar positioning, and uneven or older frames may affect balance. No capacity is stated, so keep loads modest. It should be installed level and properly aligned.

It wipes clean with a damp cloth and stores folded. Compared with the Bluestone at the same 21 x 16 inch size, it folds and looks warmer but states no more about capacity. Against the DMI at 5 pounds, it offers a larger surface.
products.bestFor: Living room use where looks and a folding tray both matter.
pros: Bamboo finish suits home decor
Folds in half for storage
21 x 16 inch surface
Damp cloth cleans it
cons: Cup holders suit lightweight cups only

buyingCriteria.explanation: A tray table only works if its slots match your handles. The NOVA needs 16.75 inches between handles, the DMI states a 16 to 19 inch range with handles no longer than 11.5 inches and 1.5 inches wide, and the Bluestone offers 11.75 x 2 inch slots. Measure your own walker before buying. A mismatch of even an inch can tilt the surface.

Ratings differ, and some are missing. The NOVA and Medline both state 10 pounds, the DMI states 5 pounds, and the Bluestone, StrongArm and Medical King publish none. Plates, drinks and a book add up, so keep the total below the rating and centered. Without a number, assume only light loads and ask a clinician.

Fold-away designs save space. The Medline flips away and the Medical King folds in half, while the NOVA, Bluestone, DMI and StrongArm are rigid. If you want the tray only at mealtimes, a folding design keeps your walker slim. The NOVA at 1.7 pounds is light enough to remove each time.

A big surface suits meals and puzzles, a small one suits a book. The NOVA gives 16 x 22.75 inches and the Bluestone and Medical King give 21 x 16 inches, while the DMI listing cites 16 x 21 style dimensions at 1 inch depth. Make sure the size does not hide the floor from you. A deeper tray extends toward you, so check your reach.

Two holders let you carry a drink and a second item. The NOVA holders are 2 7/8 inches across, the Bluestone are 2.75 inches and spaced 8.5 inches apart, and the Medical King warns about wider cups. StrongArm uses one holder placed away from hinges. Match the holder to your usual mug, and avoid heavy tumblers.

A tray changes how load sits on the frame. Medical King warns that uneven or older frames may affect balance, and DMI says weight must be evenly distributed to prevent tipping. Load slowly and keep items centered. Ask a physical therapist if the walker feels different, and do not lean on the tray.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit data
howWeEvaluated.description: We prioritized listings with measurable fit data. DMI gives a 16 to 19 inch range and handle limits, NOVA gives 16.75 inch spacing, and Bluestone gives slot sizes. StrongArm and Medline provided less to check.

howWeEvaluated.title: Load rating
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated ratings, which are 10 pounds for NOVA and Medline and 5 pounds for DMI. Picks with no rating lost points. We never filled in a limit that the maker did not state.

howWeEvaluated.title: Spill protection
howWeEvaluated.description: We reviewed edges and cup holders. NOVA, Medline and Bluestone share a half inch edge, and cup holder sizes range from 2.75 to 2 7/8 inches. Medical King admitted its holders suit light cups.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fold and storage
howWeEvaluated.description: We scored fold behavior and tray weight. Medline flips at 3 pounds, Medical King folds in half, and NOVA stays rigid at 1.7 pounds. StrongArm earned credit for keeping the holder away from hinges.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleaning and finish
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at materials and how easy they are to wipe clean. Plastic trays from NOVA, Bluestone, DMI and StrongArm wipe quickly, and bamboo from Medical King needs a damp cloth. The bamboo also scored for home appearance.

faq.q: Which tray table is best overall?
faq.a: The NOVA leads on stated capacity and surface at 10 pounds and 16 x 22.75 inches, as long as your handles are about 16.75 inches apart. The Medline matches the rating and folds away. If your walker is a different style, check the fit numbers first and ask a clinician.

faq.q: Can I put hot food on a tray table?
faq.a: Use caution. None of the listings promises heat resistance, and spills are a real risk when you walk. Keep hot drinks in sturdy cups, carry less than the stated rating and move slowly. A physical therapist can advise on safe carrying.

faq.q: Why do some listings give no weight capacity?
faq.a: Some makers simply do not publish it. The NOVA and Medline state 10 pounds and the DMI states 5 pounds, while the Bluestone, StrongArm and Medical King do not. Without a number, treat the tray as light duty only.

Most listings target standard folding walkers. The Medline and NOVA specify standard folding walkers, and the NOVA excludes 1-button paddle fold frames. Rollator handles differ, so confirm compatibility with the product page and your clinician.

faq.q: How do I clean a tray table?
faq.a: Plastic trays wipe clean with a damp cloth, and so does bamboo. Dry the surface fully and avoid soaking the bamboo. Clean the handle slots too, so the tray grips the handles evenly.

faq.q: Will a tray make my walker harder to fold?
faq.a: It can. Rigid trays such as the NOVA and Bluestone usually come off before folding, while the Medline flips and the Medical King folds in half. StrongArm says its holder sits away from hinge points, so check your own hinges before buying.

faq.q: Is a bigger tray always better?
faq.a: No. A deep tray such as the NOVA at 22.75 inches is great for a dinner plate, but it extends toward you and can limit how close you stand to the frame. A smaller tray like the DMI at 5 pounds is easier to manage for a drink and a book. Pick the size that matches what you actually carry, and have a physical therapist check how it feels while you walk.

faq.q: Can I leave the tray on all day?
faq.a: You can, if it stays level and does not interfere with doorways or hinges. Many people prefer to remove rigid trays between meals, and the NOVA at 1.7 pounds is light enough to lift on and off. Folding designs like the Medline and Medical King make it easy to keep the walker slim. If the tray rattles or tilts, remove it and recheck the fit.
